item.title: Xi's trip builds solidarity and consensus
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
Xi's trip builds solidarity and consensus Reforming, improving global governance also a key outcome, foreign minister says President Xi Jinping returned to Beijing on Thursday morning after attending the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek and concluding state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt. Officials and experts said the five-day trip, covering more than 20 bilateral and multilateral events across Central Asia and the Middle East, responded to international calls for peace, stability and development with concrete efforts, offering Chinese solutions and insights to a world of intertwined changes and turbulence. Speaking at a news briefing in Cairo upon the conclusion of the trip, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said that with solidarity and cooperation as its central theme, the trip was significant for building consensus on cooperation and for reforming and improving global governance. In Bishkek, Xi attended the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the SCO as the organization marked its 25th anniversary this year. At the summit, Xi announced that China would establish a China-SCO port economic cooperation center in Tianjin and a China-SCO basic education cooperation center, and implement 100 technological cooperation projects with other SCO countries over the next three years. Leaders of the member states signed and issued the Bishkek Declaration, approved the protocol on amendments and additions to the SCO Charter, and adopted 28 outcome documents covering areas such as security, economic and people-to-people cooperation, as well as organizational development. The strategic blueprint drawn up at last year's Tianjin summit is becoming a reality step by step, Wang said, noting that the SCO now has a more optimized structure, more efficient operation and stronger cooperation. According to Wang, in Kyrgyzstan, the two heads of state reached important consensus on further deepening the two nations' comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era and advancing the building of a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future. Bilateral relations are now at their best in history, he said. Wang said the most important political outcome of the visit was the signing of the treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation. The treaty enshrines the two countries' commitment to lasting friendship in legal form and opens broader prospects for bilateral relations, he said. Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Zheenbek Kulubaev told reporters that as a result of Monday's meeting of the heads of state, Kyrgyzstan and China have raised the strategic partnership to a high-quality level of development. This reflects the high level of political trust and confidence between the two countries and their readiness to further deepen cooperation, he said. Xi's trip to Egypt was the first state visit to the country by a Chinese president in a decade and coincided with the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations. According to Wang, Xi has emphasized that China, whether in the past, at present or in the future, is Egypt's trustworthy and dependable comprehensive strategic partner. Wang described Xi's historic visit to Egypt as both a journey to renew friendship and one to expand cooperation, calling it a milestone that fully demonstrates the strategic and exemplary nature of China-Egypt relations. Zoon Ahmed Khan, a researcher at the Belt and Road Institute of Tsinghua University, said Xi's visit reflected an ongoing transformation in which the two ancient civilizations are advancing from mere markets and transit corridors into creators of their own shared agency. "The true vitality of this partnership lies in its tangible momentum," she said, pointing to industrial hubs, local-currency financing, space technology and job-creating projects as examples of political trust being translated into productive capacity and practical South-South cooperation. Ayman Mohseb, a member of Egypt's House of Representatives, said that closer China-Egypt coordination could help ease regional tensions, promote dialogue and political settlements, and contribute to a more balanced and equitable international order. During his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Xi put forward a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East via upholding a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security. He called for fostering the internal driving force for regional security, adopting a comprehensive approach to advancing common security in the region, consolidating the foundation for common security through development and strengthening international coordination. Wang also highlighted the cultural and people-to-people dimensions. Peng Liyuan, Xi's wife, took part in cultural activities with Aigul Japarova, the wife of the Kyrgyz president, and Entissar El-Sisi, the wife of the Egyptian president. The activities added a warm cultural dimension and helped strengthen mutual understanding, people-to-people bonds and cultural exchanges, Wang said. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: One giant leap for humanoid kind
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
One giant leap for humanoid kind Industry approaches major breakthrough as Chinese companies lead advances in robot embodied intelligence Last month, global attention was focused on the futuristic feats achieved during the five-day World Humanoid Robot Games held in Beijing. Humanoid robots made in China repeatedly broke human sporting records, including Usain Bolt's 9.58 seconds in the men's 100-meter sprint and Wayde van Niekerk's 43.03 seconds in the men's 400 meters. As humanoid robots further demonstrate growing capabilities across a variety of fields, companies and professionals across the industry in China are racing to secure a leading position. At the same time, a big question is being asked: Has the "iPhone moment" for humanoid intelligence already arrived? First used in 2023 by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who referred to ChatGPT as the iPhone moment of AI, the phrase has come to describe a disruptive point when a technology or product moves from a concept to widespread adoption, bringing major changes to an industry and user experience. Wang Xingxing, founder and CEO of Unitree Robotics, one of China's best-known humanoid robot makers, remained cautious about when embodied intelligence could reach this major turning point. "Embodied intelligence could reach an industry tipping point similar to a ChatGPT moment in as little as two to three years, or perhaps five to 10 years at the slowest," Wang reportedly told the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing on Aug 20. A day earlier, Unitree made its debut on the Shanghai Stock Exchange's sci-tech innovation board, or STAR Market, closing 460 percent higher.

item.title: Visitors tune in to melody road
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
When a visitor surnamed Zhang, from Shenyang, the capital of Liaoning province, took her family for a drive on a stretch of highway in North China's Inner Mongolia autonomous region, her car's tires began to hum a melody of the grasslands. "It was so much fun!" she recalled. "I had seen videos online, but experiencing it in person was completely different. The tires rolling over the road created this beautiful tune, and my first reaction was, 'Whoa, it really works!'" Zhang said she promptly turned around and drove along the stretch again. "It's just too short — I couldn't get enough of it." What this visitor experienced was the Dada Route's new "musical road" — an 800-meter stretch of road engineered to play a melody through friction when vehicles pass at a steady speed of no more than 50 kilometers per hour. Located near the western gate of the Asgat Stone Forest scenic area in Hexigten Banner in Inner Mongolia's Chifeng, the musical stretch of road features 12,366 grooves milled precisely in the asphalt. The "musical road" is the latest addition to the 135-km Dada Route, a highway that offers one of China's most scenic drives. The route winds its way through six distinct landscapes — lakes, grasslands, sandy areas, forests, mountains and the stone forest. It is often described as a "moving encyclopedia of the grassland". In 2024, the Dada Route was named one of China's most beautiful self-driving routes — the only highway in Inner Mongolia to receive the honor awarded by the Ministry of Transport. It now welcomes more than 3 million visitors and roughly 1 million vehicles each year. The journey begins at the serene Dalai Nuur Lake, one of Inner Mongolia's four largest inland lakes and a haven for migratory birds. As the road meanders through the vast Gongger Grassland, the landscape unfolds as an endless expanse of green dotted with grazing herds of cows, sheep and horses. The route culminates at the Asgat Stone Forest, a 5A-level scenic area — the highest category in China's five-tier tourist attraction rating system — and a world geological park. Formed more than 150 million years ago through volcanic eruptions and glacial movements, the stone forest features towering, layered granite pillars. Feng Litian, deputy director of the Hexigten Banner Culture, Tourism and Sports Bureau, said that since the "musical road" opened on June 1, around 420,000 trips have been recorded along the Dada Route. More than 80 percent of visitors to the area now arrive by car, he added.

item.title: Mecca pact signals new era in regional security
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
Mecca pact signals new era in regional security The Joint Defense Agreement signed by Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in Mecca on Aug 7 signifies an important shift toward regional autonomy in West Asia's security landscape. No sooner was the agreement signed than hasty interpretations were put forth. Some labeled it a "Sunni NATO" aimed against Iran, while others saw it as a new tool in the United States-Israel regional strategy. However, facts show precisely the opposite. Rather than strengthening the US-centric security framework in West Asia, the Mecca Agreement signals its unraveling. Regional countries no longer want to rely on a single external power for their security. They are establishing their own security mechanisms despite existing tensions. The critical question is: Who will decide the future of West Asia's security? After the Gulf War, the US had promised to ensure the security of the Gulf and West Asia, establishing a massive military presence there. This led to the occupation of Iraq and Afghanistan, attempts to fragment Syria and the unresolved Palestinian question. Israel's military superiority became a permanent feature. However, all this failed to provide true security in the region. Instead, the system led to wars, terrorism, weakened states and displaced peoples. There are two distinct visions of security in West Asia. The first approach aims to make Israel a regional center, rally Arab countries around it and preserve US dominance in security affairs. But despite US backing, Israel could not oust Iran from the regional equation militarily. It also could not rally Arab nations against Iran or resolve the Palestinian question. Military superiority did not translate into political leadership. Israel's conflict in Gaza, attacks on Lebanon and Syria, and the major conflict with Iran demonstrate the futility of an Israel-centered regional order. The second approach reflects the determination of regional countries to steer their own destiny, a resolve that acquired an institutional form through the Mecca Agreement. This second path does not imply all issues with Iran have been resolved. Saudi Arabia and the other Gulf countries still have security concerns regarding Iran. The Mecca Agreement also aims to curb Iran's proxy support in neighboring countries. Turkiye and Pakistan do not want regional instability to spill over into their territories. Iran, too, will have a place in the evolving security framework inspired by the Mecca Agreement. Israel's dominance will be rejected, but its existence won't be denied. Relations with the US will be maintained, but Washington won't be seen as the sole arbiter of the region's security. The essence of the new direction is clear: No single external power should determine West Asia's destiny. The countries of the region will determine their future. The quest for a new regional order is closely linked to the reconciliation China brokered between Saudi Arabia and Iran in March 2023. The agreement reached in Beijing not only restored diplomatic ties, but also demonstrated that security can be forged through dialogue and mutual assurances, not exclusion and encirclement. While the US builds military blocs, China brings adversaries to the negotiating table. This approach embodies the Global Security Initiative proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, which emphasizes that one country's security cannot be built on another country's insecurity. The GSI advocates common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, favoring partnerships over bloc formation and dialogue over confrontation. The Mecca Agreement is not yet a full realization of these principles, but it aligns with the trend of enhancing regional ownership and reducing external dependence, while remaining open to broader participation. Turkiye has a distinctive place in this emerging order, given its stable relations with multiple countries both within and beyond the region. This is a significant opportunity. Turkiye aims to unite regional powers on common security grounds, including Iran. Ankara's long-term goal is for each country to guarantee the sovereignty, territorial integrity and security of others. The Mecca Agreement will not become a "Muslim NATO". West Asia doesn't need a new military camp or become a new front against any country. What it needs is an inclusive order in which the region's key countries — above all Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Pakistan and Egypt — recognize one another's legitimate security concerns. Palestine must be central to this order, as no security structure can be legitimate or lasting if it disregards Palestinian rights. Israel's security will be sustainable only by recognizing the right of the Palestinian people to establish a state. Security and development are inseparable. The region needs transport corridors, energy cooperation, reconstruction, trade, and water and food security. Lasting security cannot be built without jobs for young people and development opportunities for countries. This is where the Belt and Road Initiative can play a key role. The BRI is not just an infrastructure program but also a framework for cooperation that links countries' economic interests, raises the cost of external aggression and strengthens the foundations of peace. The Mecca Agreement is a work in progress. A regional security architecture has not been established yet. The priorities of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan are also not entirely aligned. Distrust between Iran and the Gulf countries persists. Egypt's place in the new mechanism has yet to be settled. The US military presence in the region continues. Israel has not abandoned its aggression. The agreement is also not a perfect solution. But it is the nucleus of a future "West Asian Union". New orders emerge if the old order cannot resolve issues. For more than a century, West Asia has paid the price of outsiders drawing their borders, imposing wars and importing security systems. Now the countries of the region are seeking an order in which they can resolve their differences of their own accord. If China's mediation experience, Turkiye's regional initiative, Saudi Arabia's diversification of its security options, Pakistan's strategic capacity, Iran's regional weight and Egypt's historical position can converge in the same constructive direction, a new era may begin in West Asia. Security cannot be imported. Peace cannot be imposed. A regional order is built through the will of regional peoples. This is the real message coming from Mecca. The author is the chairman of the Turkish-Chinese Business Development and Friendship Association. The views don't necessarily reflect those of China Daily. item.title: Serving up emotions: A chat with director Wen Muye
item.description:

In an exclusive conversation with Cultural Frontline, director Wen Muye, Egyptian teen star Omar Sherif, and talent producer Mohamed Osama, founder of Dragon Bridge Media, share the story behind the box-office hit Once Upon a Time in the Middle East. For Wen, food is one of life's simplest pleasures — making it a powerful contrast to the abnormal reality of war. From a lavish breakfast to a single fried egg, every dish in the film carries an emotion particular to that moment. The film is also a vivid example of China-Egypt cinematic collaboration. Omar, whose great-grandfather hailed from Shandong province, says his experiences in China have given him a strong sense of belonging and made him feel at home. For Mohamed, cultural exchange is key to creating stories that cross borders. He hopes to help build stronger China-Egypt ties through film and bring more compelling stories to audiences worldwide. item.title: Live: Power restored to core disaster area at Gyirong
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
President Xi Jinping urges all-out rescue, relief efforts after mudslide hits border port in Xizang Level-II emergency response activated after mudslide hits border port in Xizang Zhangmu Port in Nyalam of Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, will adjust its customs and border inspection facilities from Saturday to improve safety management for the high-altitude mountain environment, according to an announcement by the local government on Thursday. Located in a deep Himalayan valley, the port is a major land gateway between China and Nepal. Its mountainous terrain exposes the area to geological hazards. The adjustment is aimed at protecting inbound and outbound travelers and their property, while maintaining normal border clearance operations and orderly movement through the port. Starting at 10 am on Saturday, customs and immigration inspection operations at Zhangmu Port will be moved to the port's former temporary inspection area for import cargo. The road section connecting the Friendship Bridge border gate to the new inspection site will be designated as a controlled port area and a customs transit supervision zone, with closed-loop management implemented. Under the new arrangement, cross-border travelers will be transferred through designated routes. They will not be allowed to leave the designated area, move around freely, get on and off vehicles midway, or have unauthorized contact with people outside the designated transfer system. Without permission, vehicles will not be allowed to stop along the controlled section to pick up or drop off passengers or load or unload goods. Unrelated personnel and vehicles will also be barred from entering the area. Authorities said that the change only concerns the layout of customs and border inspection facilities. The port's opening status and bilateral customs clearance policies will remain unchanged. Following the glacier-collapse mudslide that struck Gyirong Port in Xizang autonomous region, China's meteorological authorities swiftly deployed portable ground-based weather observation facilities near the port, providing real-time weather support for rescue efforts. Fire and rescue teams are expanding detailed searches across the core disaster area around Gyirong Port in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, after the main land route was reopened, allowing heavy machinery to support deeper excavation and searches, the Ministry of Emergency Management said on Thursday. National Highway G216 was fully reopened to the core area on Wednesday morning. Rescue personnel, supplies and heavy equipment have since moved in, shifting operations from largely manual surface searches to deeper and more targeted searches. The State Grid announced that after power crews worked around the clock, temporary power lines to the core area of Gyirong Port were fully restored on Thursday evening, ensuring electricity supplies for rescue and relief operations in the area. The mudslide struck Gyirong Port on Aug 26 after originating on the Nepalese side of the China-Nepal border. As of noon on Wednesday, 21 victims had been found and 541 people remained missing. The disaster also knocked local base stations out of service, severed sections of main power lines and cut roads, electricity and communications to the hardest-hit area. After days of repairs, communications for emergency command, rescue operations and supply dispatch have been restored, with full 5G coverage now available in the core disaster area. Power crews are also extending electricity lines deeper into the area, local authorities said. Mud and debris in the core area average about 4 meters deep and reach up to 16 meters in some places, with large rocks covering the surface. A 195-member fire and rescue task force has been divided into three groups rotating through the core zone, focusing on areas including a parking lot and the joint inspection building. Teams are clearing and searching debris layer by layer, using life-detection equipment and search dogs to check newly exposed areas. Since the disaster, fire and rescue forces have made 336 personnel deployments and conducted repeated searches in the core area, said the Ministry of Emergency Management. Heavy machinery is clearing large rocks and deep deposits, allowing firefighters to follow behind and conduct more precise searches around buried buildings, rock piles and sediment-filled river sections. Yang Qiqiao, a firefighter with the Shigatse fire and rescue detachment who was among the first rescuers to reach the disaster area on foot, told CCTV that teams initially relied mainly on manual methods, calling out for survivors, listening for responses and knocking on debris. Search dogs and more detection equipment were added as more equipment reached the core area, he said. Secondary-disaster prevention remains a major focus. The regional authorities said 93 experts and technical personnel are monitoring barrier lakes, the source area of the ice-rock collapse and geological hazards along the road to the border gate. Monitoring continues for possible landslides and mudslides under continued rainfall and higher temperatures. About 150 pieces of professional equipment have been deployed, including 104 sets of slope radar, video monitoring, drones, water-level and meteorological equipment. Rescue sites also have dedicated safety officers, evacuation signals, escape routes and safe assembly areas prepared in advance. Search, monitoring and sanitation teams are working in shifts around the clock, with machinery continuing to operate as personnel rotate. To support road reinforcement and deeper excavation, the Ministry of Emergency Management and the Ministry of Transport have also dispatched 40 sets of temporary roadbed panels, cranes and other equipment from a national highway emergency reserve center in Changji Hui autonomous prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region. The panels help prevent excavators, cranes and dump trucks from sinking in mud and soft ground. The equipment has arrived at the rescue site. The ministry said rescue teams will continue adjusting deployments while maintaining intensive searches in the core area. Contact the writers at yangzekun@chinadaily.com.cn Twenty-one people have been confirmed dead, and 541 remain missing after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in Xizang autonomous region on Aug 26, according to the regional government's latest news briefing. The mudslide began with the collapse of a high-altitude glacier in Nepal, which triggered an ice-rock avalanche that developed into a fast-moving debris flow before reaching the port. The disaster has brought renewed attention to the Himalayan valley in which Gyirong sits. Gyirong is one of the main land gateways between China and Nepal. Its geography made it a natural passage between the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau and South Asia. It has been used for more than 1,000 years. Long before the establishment of a modern border crossing, the route carried royal missions, diplomats, religious masters, and traders. In the seventh century, Nepali Princess Bhrikuti traveled through Gyirong on her way to marry Tibetan King Songtsan Gampo. The Buddha statue she was said to have brought was enshrined at Phakpa Lhakhang Temple in modern-day Gyirong county. The same century also saw Tang Dynasty (618-907) envoy Wang Xuance pass through the area on a mission to India in 658. Wang left a cliff inscription as a record of the journey that survives today. In the eighth century, Indian Buddhist master Padmasambhava also traveled through Gyirong, which was described as the first stop on his mission, as he entered Xizang to teach Buddhism. Together, these journeys illustrate Gyirong's long-standing role as a corridor for exchanges between the plateau and South Asia. That role continued into modern times. Gyirong was designated a national first-class land port in 1978 and opened to travelers from third countries in 2017, becoming an important gateway for cross-border travel and trade. The port saw imports and exports worth 4.25 billion yuan ($632.6 million) in 2024, ranking first among ports in the region and accounting for nearly 30 percent of the total China-Nepal trade volume, according to Xinhua News Agency. The mudslide disrupted access through the border area. By Wednesday, road access to the core disaster zone had been largely restored, allowing rescuers and heavy machinery to move in and help with the search for those still missing. Temporary power supply lines to the core disaster area around Gyirong Port in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, were fully restored by Thursday evening, ensuring electricity for ongoing search and rescue operations, the China Central Television reported. Power crews had been working around the clock to repair damaged lines since a massive mudslide struck Gyirong Port on Aug 26, cutting off roads, electricity and communications in the hardest-hit area. The restoration of power follows progress in reopening transport and communications links to the disaster zone. National Highway G216, the main land route to Gyirong Port, was fully reopened on Wednesday morning, allowing rescuers, relief supplies and heavy equipment to enter the core area and support deeper searches. Communications have also been restored after crews laid fiber-optic cables, repaired faults, restored base stations and optimized signals. According to local authorities, emergency command, rescue operations and supply dispatch now have uninterrupted communications, while the core disaster area has achieved full 5G coverage. Emergency road reinforcement equipment has been dispatched to Gyirong county in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, to support road access and enhance search operations following last week's devastating mudslide, the Ministry of Emergency Management announced on Thursday. Through an emergency coordination mechanism between the Ministry of Emergency Management and the Ministry of Transport, 40 sets of temporary roadbed panels, cranes, and other essential equipment were urgently allocated from a national regional highway emergency equipment reserve center in Changji Hui autonomous prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region. Escorted by Xinjiang regional transport authorities, the equipment has now arrived at the rescue site. The temporary roadbed panels are specifically designed for use on mud, soft soil, and other unstable ground, helping to prevent heavy machinery like excavators, cranes, and dump trucks from sinking by distributing their weight. This equipment is urgently required to reinforce damaged roads and support deeper excavation and search operations in the mudslide-affected area, according to the ministry. The massive mudslide, originating on the Nepalese side of the China-Nepal border, struck Gyirong Port on Aug 26, resulting in significant casualties and leaving many people missing. The disaster severely damaged National Highway G216, the main road to the port, complicating access to the core disaster area. Rescue teams have been working to restore and reinforce the land route while expanding search efforts in areas covered by deep mud and debris. A mudslide struck Gyirong Port in Shigatse on Aug 26 after originating on the Nepalese side of China-Nepal border. It caused major casualties and damaged roads, electricity and communications, cutting off access to the core disaster area. After days of continuous efforts, National Highway G216, the main route to the port, reopened on Wednesday. China Daily reporter Palden Nyima is on-site at G216, providing live updates on the latest developments. Tune in to watch the efforts LIVE. A food truck has been deployed in mudslide-affected Gyirong town of Gyirong county recently, providing hot meals to disaster relief volunteers. The truck came from the neighboring Dingri county. After being hit by an earthquake in 2025, Dingri county purchased the truck with funds from East China's Shanghai under an assistance program for Xizang. After Gyirong town was hit by the mudslide, Dingri county soon dispatched the truck to share mobile food services for disaster relief. The death toll from the mudslide at a China-Nepal border port rose to 21 on Wednesday, authorities said, while 541 people remained missing as rescuers expanded deep searches in the disaster's core area after restoring a key land route. Karma Tsetan, chairman of the government of the Xizang autonomous region, gave the figures at a news conference in Gyirong on Wednesday, saying more than 2,300 rescuers had been mobilized for the operation. The mudslide struck Gyirong Port in Shigatse on Aug 26 after originating on the Nepalese side of the border. It caused major casualties and damaged roads, electricity and communications, cutting off access to the core disaster area. The reopening of a section of National Highway G216, the main road leading to the port, has allowed rescuers to move heavy machinery into the hardest-hit areas and intensify searches for people buried beneath thick layers of mud and debris. Karma Tsetan said more than 400 vehicle deployments and more than 8,000 sets of rescue equipment had been mobilized. Drones had made about 800 flights, while 5.43 metric tons of personnel supplies and equipment had been air-dropped into the core area. Before the road was restored, rescuers relied on a combination of land, water and air operations to reach the disaster zone. Some teams approached by boat along waterways, while others trekked for about 12 hours through mountainous terrain. Helicopters made 24 flights to transport rescuers and supplies. Communications have also improved, with 12 base stations restored and lighting and power equipment deployed in the core area, Karma Tsetan said. Rescuers have carried out repeated grid searches covering about 1.59 million square meters since the disaster. More than 10 pieces of heavy machinery have now entered the core area, enabling teams to move from surface searches to more extensive excavation. Ren Wei, executive vice-chairman of the Xizang regional government, said the latest searches are focusing on deeper layers of debris, with mud deposits averaging about 4 meters and reaching as deep as 16 meters in some locations. Large rocks and thick mud have covered the surface, making it difficult to determine what lies underneath, Ren said. Rescue teams have divided the affected area into sections and are using professional detection equipment to search beneath the debris. Priority is being given to locations where people may have been trapped, including a parking lot, a joint inspection building and accommodation buildings. The Ministry of Emergency Management said firefighters have adjusted their strategy as heavy equipment becomes available. Excavators are being used to clear large quantities of debris, while specialized teams conduct detailed searches and use life-detection equipment at targeted locations. Searches are also focusing on buried buildings, riverbanks, gullies and damaged sections of road. Search dogs and life detectors are being used where conditions permit. A forward command post has been established about 1.5 kilometers from Gyirong Port to improve coordination among teams operating close to the disaster area. Yao Xueqin, a member of a Lhasa fire and rescue mobile detachment, said the high-altitude location and extensive damage to roads and communications had made the operation particularly difficult. Thin air, steep slopes and deep mud quickly exhaust rescuers, while damaged roads initially forced teams to rely heavily on walking and drones to move personnel and supplies, Yao said. Disrupted communications also made it difficult for commanders to track teams and issue warnings in real time. Fog, rain and turbulent air currents in the valleys have periodically restricted drone flights and aerial supply operations. The mudslide also drastically changed the terrain and erased familiar landmarks, adding to the difficulties of locating missing people. The reopening of G216 had been a major priority for rescue authorities. Karma Tsetan said crews worked around the clock despite narrow working areas, unstable slopes, rapidly rising water, deep mud and continuing rainfall. A total of 1,333 personnel deployments and 658 equipment deployments were made during the road-reopening operation. By 10 am on Wednesday, the route into the core area had been largely restored, allowing personnel, supplies and heavy machinery to enter by land. China Anneng Group, a national force for disaster engineering rescue and infrastructure construction, said it had deployed 158 rescuers and 33 pieces of equipment on Tuesday night to reinforce water-damaged sections of G216. Crews worked through heavy rain to strengthen temporary roadbeds while monitoring river levels and surrounding slopes. The risk of secondary disasters remains a major concern. More rain is forecast in Gyirong over the next three days, according to the China Meteorological Administration. Three national emergency rescue teams, comprising 39 personnel, have formed a joint monitoring group, the Ministry of Emergency Management said. The teams have accumulated 120 hours of monitoring and collected about 2,700 sets of data on barrier lakes, landslide areas and unstable slopes. Rockfall radar, slope radar and other equipment are monitoring the surrounding mountains, gullies and debris deposits around the clock. Meteorological authorities are providing detailed forecasts every six hours. Yao said rescuers have been instructed to prioritize safety, with teams withdrawing from low-lying valley areas at night and operating in groups with rope protection. Personnel have been told to evacuate immediately if monitoring systems detect signs of danger. Chinese meteorological and water authorities have stepped up cooperation with Nepal following the deadly mudslide that struck the two countries' border, sharing monitoring data and providing weather and hydrological forecasts to support rescue efforts. The Aug 26 disaster originated on the Nepalese side of the border and severely affected Gyirong Port in the Xizang autonomous region. The area's high altitude, complex terrain and rapidly changing weather conditions have made rescue operations particularly challenging. "From late August to early September, plateau shear lines and low vortices are frequently active along the border, with frequent precipitation, posing serious challenges to rescue work," said Ma Xuekuan, chief forecaster at the National Meteorological Center. Following a request from Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology around noon on Aug 26, the China Meteorological Administration organized an emergency joint consultation with its Nepalese counterpart that afternoon. A second consultation was held on Aug 31, according to Zhang Tianhang, a senior engineer at the World Meteorological Centre Beijing. The two sides also established a WeChat working group for real-time information sharing, allowing them to respond quickly to requests during the emergency. The consultations used MAZU, a Chinese cloud-based early warning system, to jointly assess weather conditions and forecast precipitation in the affected area. China subsequently established a dedicated meteorological support team for Nepal and began providing daily monitoring and forecasting reports in English. "Overall, we have provided seamless forecasting services covering the next 30 days, offering strong support for Nepal's rescue operations," Zhang said. China has also provided Nepal with a customized version of MAZU. Nepal has since requested additional functions, including lightning monitoring, subseasonal to seasonal forecasts and more detailed monitoring and forecasting products. Chinese authorities have shared a range of meteorological products and observational data through the customized version of MAZU, Zhang said. Water authorities have also joined the effort. A barrier lake formed near the confluence of Nepal's Cuojian River and China's Purepu Tsangpo River following the disaster. The Ministry of Water Resources immediately sent a hydrological emergency monitoring team to the area, working with Xizang's regional hydrological and water resources survey authorities. Chinese authorities are providing Nepal with daily updates in five areas, including the development of the barrier lake; potential chain risks from impact pits along the Cuojian River; risks from glacial lakes in the Gyirong Zangbo basin; the development and risk forecasts of newly formed barrier lakes; and emergency hydrological monitoring information. The information is intended to help Nepal assess risks and organize rescue efforts downstream, according to the ministry. Following the disaster, the CMA mobilized resources from the national to local levels. A small ground weather station was installed near the disaster area on the night of Aug 26 and a mobile weather radar was deployed nearby on Sept 1. "These facilities have supplemented our understanding of local weather conditions and improved the precision and accuracy of local forecasts," Ma said. zhaoyimeng@chinadaily.com.cn Ma Hua, an emergency responder from Lhasa, Xizang autonomous region, typically handles air transfers of critically ill patients and provides basic medical care. But in mudslide-stricken Gyirong county, he took on a very different role: cooking three meals a day for medical staff, truck drivers and other rescue workers. After arriving in Gyirong, Shigatse city, following the Aug 26 mudslide, Ma and his team found that there was limited demand for air ambulance services. Instead, they learned that a catering vehicle deployed by the Red Cross Society of Xizang Autonomous Region needed extra hands in the kitchen. "I used to work as a cook and have supported disaster relief in that role before," Ma said from the Xizang 999 Emergency Rescue Center. "So our team quickly got in touch with the Red Cross and shifted roles." The catering vehicle, parked at a hospital where local medical staff and doctors dispatched from other regions are working, began providing three free meals a day on Sunday and has so far served more than 1,500 portions. Tseyang, deputy director of the Xizang Red Cross Society's relief and rescue department, said the hospital's kitchen was relatively small and had only one cook. Following the devastating mudslide, regional and national authorities dispatched medical aid teams, including emergency care specialists, orthopedists and psychologists, to help provide medical treatment and mental health support. "We Red Cross workers, along with seven emergency responders like Ma, have worked together to ensure adequate meal supplies for them and ease the burden on the hospital," she said. Demand varies from day to day, Tseyang said. The kitchen has been operating at full capacity, with extra portions packed into food containers for distribution to those in need. At around 1:30 pm on Wednesday, Tseyang and two coworkers loaded dozens of servings of freshly cooked dishes onto a vehicle and set out to find truck drivers, loaders and sanitation workers resting on the streets. One driver, who had transported rocks and gabions to the hardest-hit Gyirong Port, said that although he had already eaten lunch, the meals offered by the Red Cross looked so appealing that he gladly shared them with other drivers taking a break at the curbside. "They do manual labor and burn a lot of energy, so they really need the extra food," Tseyang said. For Qi Youpeng, another medical worker from the Xizang 999 Emergency Rescue Center, helping in the kitchen was also a departure from his usual role. He typically provides first aid during rescue missions, including after the magnitude-6.2 earthquake that struck Jishishan county in Gansu province in December 2023. Now, he washes and chops vegetables and helps prepare meals aboard the catering vehicle. "I'll go wherever I'm needed and I am willing to help in any way," he said. Contact the writers at wangxiaoyu@chinadaily.com.cn In the aftermath of the mudslide that struck Gyirong Port in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, psychological support for the families of the deceased and missing, as well as local residents and rescue workers, has been prioritized, officials announced on Wednesday. Following the landslide on Aug 26, Shigatse authorities swiftly formed a response team and developed a comprehensive plan to manage the aftermath, proactively reaching out to the families of the missing, said Wang Fanghong, deputy head of the disaster emergency and rescue command headquarters and Communist Party of China chief of Shigatse. So far, 587 family members have received accommodation and assistance, including 253 cases related to domestic individuals reported as missing or deceased, Wang revealed. A team of 70 professionals has been assigned to provide psychological counseling to these families, offering care and assistance 1,107 times. Additionally, 1,220 personnel have been organized to support these services, he added. Four dedicated phone lines have also been established to offer consultation services to families of missing and deceased individuals both domestically and internationally. These lines have received 876 calls — 448 from China and 428 from abroad — with all inquiries documented for follow-up responses, Wang said. "Ongoing care and support will be provided to the families of the deceased and missing," he added. Tan Xiangdong, Party chief of the Xizang autonomous regional health commission, emphasized the importance of psychological support, acknowledging the deep trauma caused by the mudslide. "We have prioritized psychological support by developing plans for counseling and crisis intervention," he said, noting tailored mental health services are being provided to address the specific needs of different affected groups. In collaboration with the National Health Commission and other provinces and cities, over 210 psychological assistance experts have been selected and are on standby to respond to the needs of the disaster-stricken areas, ensuring the sustainability of psychological aid, he said. Local medical professionals, particularly Tibetan doctors, have been leveraged, and specialists with strong foreign language skills have been appointed to communicate with the families of missing foreign nationals, he added. Psychological support is also being provided to local residents and rescue workers. At each disaster relocation site, Tan said, at least four medical staff have been assigned to ensure the presence of healthcare professionals, disease control personnel, mobile medical services, medication availability, and psychological care. "A bilingual Chinese-Tibetan pocket guide for psychological self-help has been developed to address various post-disaster stress reactions," he specified. "Interventions are conducted through listening, companionship, guidance and comfort, with one-on-one interventions and continuous follow-ups provided for specific families." As of noon Wednesday, a total of 966 psychological comfort and emotional support sessions had been conducted for the residents at the relocation sites, he revealed. For rescue workers, psychological risk assessments are conducted promptly, providing necessary group and individual counseling. A pocket guide for psychological self-help specifically for front-line rescue workers has been developed to help them understand emergency responses and how to manage them, he said, adding that a hotline — 12356 — has also been established for psychological services. Contact the writers at caoyin@chinadaily.com.cn Rescue teams are intensifying deep searches in the core disaster area around Gyirong Port in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, where mudslide deposits reach up to 16 meters in some places. The main land route into the area was largely restored on Wednesday morning. Follow live updates from China Daily's on-site reports. Chinese meteorological and water authorities have stepped up cooperation with Nepal following the deadly mudslide that struck the China-Nepal border, sharing monitoring data and providing weather and hydrological forecasts to support rescue efforts. Following a request from Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology around noon on Aug 26, the China Meteorological Administration organized an emergency joint consultation with its Nepalese counterpart that afternoon. A second consultation was held on Aug 31, according to Zhang Tianhang, a senior engineer at the World Meteorological Center, Beijing. The consultations used MAZU, a cloud-based early warning system, to jointly assess weather conditions and forecast precipitation in the affected area. China has also provided Nepal with a customized version of MAZU. Nepal has since requested additional functions, including lightning monitoring, subseasonal-to-seasonal forecasts and more detailed monitoring and forecasting products. Chinese authorities have shared a range of meteorological products and observation data through the customized version of MAZU, Zhang said. Following the disaster, the CMA mobilized resources from the national to local levels. A small ground weather station was installed near the disaster area on the night of Aug 26, and a mobile weather radar was deployed nearby on Sept 1. Rescue teams at Gyirong Port in the Xizang autonomous region will maintain round-the-clock searches in the core disaster area while adjusting deployments as risks evolve and strengthening monitoring of secondary disasters, evacuation planning and logistical support, regional authorities said on Wednesday. Wang Haitao, head of the Xizang Fire and Rescue Corps, said at a news conference that high-altitude protection and psychological support for rescuers would also be strengthened. As of noon on Wednesday, 21 victims had been found, 847 personal belongings had been recovered and 541 people remained missing. The mudslide struck Gyirong Port in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, on Aug 26 after originating on the Nepalese side of the China-Nepal border. It cut off roads to the hardest-hit area and exposed rescuers to steep terrain, deep mud and the risks of rockfalls, landslides and barrier lakes. Before the main land route was restored, fire and rescue teams used coordinated land, water and air operations to reach the disaster zone, Wang said. An advance team descended more than 500 meters by rope and reached the core area at 4:30 pm on Aug 28, where it established a forward command post. Rescuers then divided the area into grids and conducted repeated searches using manual excavation, search dogs, detection equipment and machinery. Waterborne teams searched riverbanks and sediment-filled sections, while drones conducted reconnaissance and helicopters supported personnel rotation and supply deliveries. With road access restored, operations have shifted from reaching the core area to conducting deeper searches. An additional 65 firefighters and more than 200 pieces of equipment have joined an initial force of 24 rescuers and two search dogs. Teams are now searching from the surface into deeper debris, focusing on areas around the border gate, collapsed structures, thick mud deposits, river valleys and other hard-to-reach locations. Fire and rescue teams are mainly responsible for two key areas — the customs accommodation building and a parking lot. A 195-member task force has been divided into three rotating groups to conduct layer-by-layer searches, clearing debris and checking each newly exposed section before moving deeper. Large machinery is being used to open up working areas, while firefighters, search dogs and detection equipment conduct more precise searches. Geological and water resources experts are continuing real-time risk assessments, while teams monitor landslides, barrier lakes and other potential secondary hazards. Wang said rescue forces would continue adjusting deployments, maintaining day-and-night shifts, refining evacuation plans and coordinating heavy machinery and helicopter support. They will also strengthen logistical support, personal protection and psychological services for rescuers engaged in prolonged operations. Rescue teams are intensifying deep searches in the core disaster area around Gyirong Port in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, where mudslide deposits reach up to 16 meters in some places. The main land route into the area was largely restored on Wednesday morning, regional authorities reported. As of noon Wednesday, 21 people had been found dead and 541 remained missing, according to Karma Tsetan, chairman of the Xizang regional government. Additionally, 847 personal belongings have been recovered. Originating on the Nepalese side of the China-Nepal border, the mudslide struck Gyirong Port on Aug 26, severing roads, electricity, and communications. Karma Tsetan stated that over 2,300 rescuers had been mobilized, supported by more than 400 vehicle deployments and over 8,000 sets of rescue equipment. Drones have conducted 804 flights, while 5.43 metric tons of supplies and equipment have been air-dropped into the core area. Prior to the restoration of the land route, rescuers advanced by water, land, and air. Boats approached the core zone via waterways, land teams trekked for about 12 hours along mountain routes, and helicopters made 24 flights to transport rescuers and supplies. Communications have improved with 12 base stations restored, and lighting and power equipment deployed in the core area, Karma Tsetan said. Rescuers have conducted repeated grid searches covering about 1.59 million square meters since the disaster. More than 10 pieces of heavy machinery have now entered the core area to support deeper searches. Reopening National Highway G216 was a major priority. Karma Tsetan noted that rescue teams worked tirelessly despite narrow working areas, unstable slopes, fast-rising water, deep mud, and continued rainfall. Rescue forces will continue coordinating searches, road restoration, recovery work, and risk prevention as operations progress deeper into the disaster zone, he said. Ren Wei, executive vice-chairman of the Xizang regional government, said search operations are now focusing on deeper layers of debris. Mudslide deposits in the core area average about 4 meters in depth, reaching up to 16 meters in some places, with large rocks and thick mud covering the surface. Rescuers have divided the area into sections and are using professional detection equipment to search beneath the debris. Priority is given to key locations, including a parking lot, the joint inspection building, and accommodation buildings. As searches move deeper, authorities are enhancing precautions against secondary disasters. Rockfall radar, slope radar, and other equipment are monitoring surrounding mountains, gullies, and debris deposits around the clock, while meteorological authorities provide detailed forecasts every six hours. Each search site has a dedicated safety officer, with evacuation signals, escape routes, and safe assembly areas prepared in advance. Ren said remains found during searches are being transferred and identified, while recovered personal belongings are catalogued, preserved, and handed over according to established procedures. Health and sanitation measures are also ongoing in the affected area. Moderate rainfall was forecast for the mudslide-devastated Gyirong Port area in China's Xizang autonomous region on Wednesday as rescue efforts proceed in the wake of the deadly natural disaster along the China-Nepal border, with major hidden risks still present in nearby watercourses. The total accumulated precipitation is expected to reach 30 to 50 millimeters, with rainfall expected to last until Friday, the ministry said in a media release on Wednesday. It said the rainfall is likely to push up water levels along the Gyirong Tsangpo River, raising the flow rate in the Gyirong Port section of the watercourse to about 150 to 300 cubic meters per second. The ministry didn't disclose the current flow rate in the section, but said a monitoring station 7 kilometers upstream of the port stood at 91.7 cubic meters per second at 1 pm on Wednesday. The ministry urged frontline rescue personnel in the area to closely monitor real-time rainfall and changes in river conditions. Workers were advised to prepare in advance for evacuation and flood-risk mitigation. The ministry warned that, based on consistent drone monitoring and satellite imagery analysis, there remain major hidden risks around the mudslide-stricken area. It said glaciers around a nearby scour pit in Nepal's Chhochen Khola River, which converges with the Purepu Tsangpo River in China, face potential collapse. It said small-scale landslides have been detected along the downstream reach of a barrier lake on the Purepu Tsangpo, heightening the risk of slope collapse that may form new barrier lakes. According to authorities, the mudslide originating in Nepal has left 21 dead and 541 missing in the port. Following the landslide on Aug 26, Shigatse authorities swiftly formed a response team and developed a comprehensive plan to manage the aftermath, proactively reaching out to the families of the missing, according to Wang Fanghong, deputy head of the disaster emergency and rescue command headquarters and Party secretary of Shigatse. So far, 587 family members of missing or deceased individuals have been accommodated and assisted, Wang revealed. A team of 70 professionals has been assigned to provide psychological counseling to these families, offering care and assistance 1,107 times. Additionally, 1,220 personnel have been organized to support these services, according to him. "A bilingual Chinese-Tibetan pocket guide for psychological self-help has been developed to address various post-disaster stress reactions," he specified. "Interventions are conducted through listening, companionship, guidance, and comfort, with one-on-one interventions and continuous follow-ups provided for specific families." As of Wednesday noon, a total of 966 psychological comfort and emotional support sessions have been conducted for the residents at the relocation sites, he revealed. For rescue workers, psychological risk assessments are conducted promptly, providing necessary group and individual counseling. A pocket guide for psychological self-help specifically for frontline rescue workers has been developed to help them understand emergency responses and how to manage them, he said, adding that a hotline — 12356 — has also been established for psychological services. Authorities in the Xizang autonomous region have intensified monitoring and early warning efforts against secondary disasters following the recent mudslide at Gyirong Port, deploying experts and specialized equipment to guard against further collapses, landslides and debris flows. Karma Tsetan, chairman of the regional government and head of the emergency rescue headquarters, said 93 experts and technical personnel are monitoring the barrier lake and the source area of the ice-rock avalanche. Geological hazards along roads leading to the border port are also being investigated, while rainfall, temperature and water-level changes in key river basins are being closely monitored to protect rescue personnel downstream. The barrier lake had discharged naturally by Aug 30, removing the immediate threat, while a small body of water formed by the ice-rock avalanche had also drained, Karma Tsetan said. About 150 sets of specialized equipment have been deployed, including 104 sets of radar, video surveillance, drones, and hydrological and meteorological monitoring devices. The Aug 26 disaster had left 21 people dead and 541 missing as of Wednesday noon. Chen Fuqi, chief engineer of the regional Department of Natural Resources, said the area's steep terrain, complex geological conditions and high-altitude hazard sources make early detection difficult. Authorities will integrate satellite remote sensing, drone surveys and ground monitoring, while strengthening geological hazard surveys, early warning, emergency coordination and cross-border information sharing, Chen said.

item.title: HK's super connector role highlighted
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
HK's super connector role highlighted High-level officials and society leaders gathered in Hong Kong on Thursday for a major conference on integration of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, with keynote speakers highlighting the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region's role as a "super connector" between the Chinese mainland and global markets amid rapidly shifting geopolitical and technological landscapes. The conference, themed "New Dynamics in Asia-Pacific Cooperation, New Opportunities for GBA Connectivity", was co-organized by China Daily and the Hong Kong Coalition, bringing together nearly 300 government officials, consuls general, business leaders and representatives from think tanks, academia and media, as well as public-private sector experts from across Asia. Leung Chun-ying, vice-chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, said that collaborative initiatives unveiled recently in data and healthcare between Hong Kong and Nansha in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, underscore the unique role of Hong Kong as a partner and super connector linking the Greater Bay Area with the rest of the world. He said the steps to be taken are clear and necessary — to promote better government-to-business and business-to-business interactions between Hong Kong and Guangdong. "The new momentum generated in recent months through cooperation between Guangdong cities in the Greater Bay Area and Hong Kong will benefit other Asia-Pacific countries and regions," Leung said. Hong Kong SAR Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu said in a video speech that the Greater Bay Area is fast becoming one of the most dynamic and integrated economic powerhouses in the world, underscoring Hong Kong's role as the only world city that converges both the China advantage and the global advantage. Lee said that this role takes on new significance this year, as the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen, Guangdong, in November, a historic first for the Greater Bay Area, and Hong Kong will host the APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting in October. He added that the region is ready for the spotlight. Lee said that Hong Kong has a deep and liquid market and a strong pool of financial and professional talent, and the city has become Asia's premier fundraising, asset management and risk management hub. He said the Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Cooperation Zone is key to turning cutting-edge ideas into tangible outcomes and world-class research into products, by bringing together Hong Kong's research excellence and the Chinese mainland's advanced manufacturing capabilities. He added that talent is central to Hong Kong's innovation and technology push, while highlighting the "one town, five elements" framework for the Northern Metropolis University Town Area — a hub where universities, research institutes and industries will be set up together to integrate the five elements of education, technology, talent, industry and urban development. "Integrating into and serving overall national development, Hong Kong brings together ideas, capital and talent across boundaries, and connects the Greater Bay Area with global markets. Together, we are not just building the Greater Bay Area. We are shaping a more connected, innovative and prosperous future," Lee said. Qu Yingpu, publisher and editor-in-chief of China Daily, said that the China Daily Hong Kong Edition has chronicled Hong Kong's remarkable voyage — enduring storms, celebrating triumphs and now recording a new era of transformation from stability to prosperity, aligned with the vibrant rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. "Amid shifting communication landscapes and unprecedented global change, we will continue to share the living story of and contribute to this 'one country, two systems', the dynamism of the Greater Bay Area and China's unwavering commitment to an open global economy," he said. Qu also said that he believes that Hong Kong will continue to innovate, leap forward and forge new heights of achievement with its first five-year plan, which is scheduled to be published on Sept 16. Hong Kong SAR Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po stressed connectivity and Hong Kong's role in connecting the world in an age of profound change driven by geopolitics and technological transformation. "As the country's most internationally connected region, the Greater Bay Area presents a strong value proposition for Asia-Pacific collaboration," Chan said. "It rests on a simple conviction: When we partner, we do not merely add up our strengths — we multiply them and extend their reach well beyond Asia." The conference also featured three panel discussions on Hong Kong's financial opportunities in the changing Asia-Pacific landscape, the synergy in commercial aerospace development between the HKSAR and Shenzhen, and education in the artificial intelligence era. Panelists highlighted how Hong Kong can seize opportunities arising from deeper Asia-Pacific economic and trade cooperation to enhance its influence as a global financial hub. Discussions also centered on harnessing the Greater Bay Area's manufacturing capabilities and Hong Kong's strengths, exploring ways to build a collaborative commercial space ecosystem. Panelists also examined how the education sector can reinvent its model with AI to cultivate talent that serves the Greater Bay Area and the Asia-Pacific market.

item.title: President calls for dialogue between civilizations
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
President calls for dialogue between civilizations President Xi Jinping emphasized the need for China and Egypt to jointly promote equality, dialogue, mutual learning and inclusiveness between civilizations during a visit to the Grand Egyptian Museum on Wednesday. Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, toured the museum accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife, Entissar El-Sisi, before leaving Cairo for Beijing. The sprawling museum stands within sight of the Pyramids of Giza, and brings together some of the most important relics and artifacts from the ancient Egyptian civilization. Cultural exchanges between China and Egypt have flourished in recent years, from major exhibitions of ancient Egyptian artifacts in China to joint archaeological projects in Egypt. El-Sisi and his wife extended a warm welcome to Xi and Peng upon their arrival at the museum. They entered the main hall of the museum together and posed for a photo in front of the colossal monolith of King Ramesses II, before listening to an introduction to the museum and the history of ancient Egypt. They admired the exquisite stone statues, inscribed stone columns and a pyramidion from a temple, before stopping at the observation deck to take in the view of the pyramids in the distance. Xi and El-Sisi also visited the Tutankhamun Galleries, where they appreciated prized collections including the pharaoh's world-famous gold burial mask, gold throne and war chariots. Noting that China and Egypt are both ancient civilizations and countries rich in World Heritage sites, Xi said that across time and space, the two civilizations have been reaching out to each other and writing new chapters of everlasting friendship between the two peoples. Xi called on the two countries to uphold the vision of civilization based on equality, mutual learning, dialogue and inclusiveness, and implement the Global Civilization Initiative. He also urged both sides to promote inclusiveness, coexistence and mutual learning among different civilizations, thereby drawing greater strength from civilizations to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. El-Sisi thanked Xi for sending a congratulatory message on the opening of the museum in Giza in November last year. He noted that ancient Egyptian and Chinese civilizations share the qualities of openness, inclusiveness and harmonious coexistence amid diversity, which closely aligns with the vision of the Global Civilization Initiative proposed by Xi. Egypt stands ready to strengthen people-to-people and cultural exchanges with China, promote mutual learning among civilizations, and help make the world more harmonious and inclusive, he said.
